brief: The Fed delivered its first hike since 2023, shifting priced expectations from roughly four cuts to near five hikes, but fiscal policy, not monetary policy, is now the dominant driver of growth and inflation. September's composite PMI hit 58.4, the strongest in five years, with input-cost inflation at its highest since October 2022, matching S&P Global's and the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow estimates of around 5% annualized growth. The CBO's $1.9tn deficit (5.8% of GDP) and debt rising from 101% to 120% of GDP by 2036 pushed 10y yields above 5.10% and 30y above 5.40% despite the hike, exporting a higher discount rate globally: France faces a debt-sustainability problem and the UK stagflation, each lacking an AI-capex offset. Separately, frontier AI capability still outruns diffusion (Copilot's roughly 10% penetration of its addressable base), so falling token prices broaden compute demand rather than shrink it. In the US-China AI race, the US leads on frontier models, but China's robotics base (54% of 2024 installations) and planned sixfold US power-capacity growth over five years could let it deploy AI more effectively, especially if a mishandled safety debate keeps raising the cost of US power and permission.
